steps.title: Grow Arabidopsis plants
steps.instruction: Prepare semi‑sterile soil by heating at 80 °C for 8 h, fill 10 cm pots, water, and sow 6–10 seeds per pot in four corners and centre. Cover with a plastic dome, stratify at 4 °C for 2 days, then transfer to a short‑day growth cabinet (8 h light/16 h dark) at 22 °C, 65 % RH, light intensity 120–140 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹. Remove dome after 3–4 days, grow 7–10 days, thin to five plants per pot, and continue until the desired stage (e.g., 6‑week‑old leaves).

steps.title: Prepare alcohol‑insoluble residue (AIR)
steps.instruction: Flash‑freeze harvested organs (leaves, stems, roots, rosettes) in liquid nitrogen; gently wash off soil debris with sterile Milli‑Q water. Optionally keep plants in darkness for 48 h to reduce starch. Grind frozen tissue to a fine powder while keeping it frozen (mortar‑pestle or ball mill). Store ground material at –80 °C (pause point). Transfer up to 100 mg ground tissue to a pre‑cooled 2 mL microcentrifuge tube, keep on ice, add 1.5 mL 70 % (v/v) ethanol, vortex, centrifuge 18 000 × g for 10 min at room temperature, discard supernatant. Repeat the ethanol wash once more. Add 1 mL chloroform / methanol (1:1, v/v), vortex, centrifuge 18 000 × g for 10 min, discard supernatant; repeat this chloroform/methanol wash two additional times (total three washes). If the pellet remains green, perform extra chloroform/methanol washes. Add 1 mL acetone, vortex, centrifuge 18 000 × g for 10 min, discard supernatant. Air‑dry the resulting AIR overnight at room temperature in a dust‑free environment. Optionally perform an α‑amylase digest to remove starch.

steps.title: Extract and hydrolyze pectin from AIR
steps.instruction: Weigh 2 mg AIR into a 2 mL microcentrifuge tube (record exact weight). Add 1.4 mL ultrapure water and two 5 mm glass beads, then homogenise with a ball mill for 1.5 min at 30 Hz. Incubate the tube for 2 h at 90 °C with vigorous shaking (speed #4 on HLC‑HTM 130). Remove from the heating block and let debris settle for 5 min (do not centrifuge). Transfer 1 mL of the supernatant to a DURAN® glass culture tube with screw cap. Dry the aliquot under a stream of N₂ gas at 50 °C (drying may be prolonged). Add 300 µL of 2 M trifluoroacetic acid (TFA) (wear gloves, goggles, work in fume hood). Hydrolyse for 1 h at 121 °C in a heating block. Evaporate TFA under N₂ stream. Add 500 µL ultrapure water and 100 µL of internal standard solution (0.05 mg mL⁻¹ allo‑inositol). Store dissolved hydrolysates at –20 °C if not processed immediately (pause point).

steps.title: Extract and hydrolyze pectin from mucilage
steps.instruction: Weigh 5 mg dry seeds into a 2 mL microcentrifuge tube (record exact mass). Add 1.4 mL ultrapure water, vortex briefly, and place on a rotary shaker for 2 h to extract mucilage. Allow seeds to settle for 1–2 min (do not centrifuge) and transfer 1 mL of the supernatant to a DURAN® glass tube. Dry under a stream of N₂ gas at 50 °C. Add 300 µL of 2 M TFA, hydrolyse 1 h at 121 °C, evaporate TFA under N₂, then add 500 µL water and 100 µL of 0.05 mg mL⁻¹ allo‑inositol. Store at –20 °C if needed. The downstream steps are identical to those for AIR extracts.

steps.title: Prepare monosaccharide standards for GC‑MS
steps.instruction: From the stock solutions (250 mM each), prepare calibration mixes by combining appropriate volumes of diluted stocks to obtain defined molar amounts (e.g., 1 nmol each: 4 µL of 1/1000 dilution). Add 5 µL of 0.05 mg mL⁻¹ allo‑inositol to each mix. For low‑abundance sugars prepare 3–5 mixes ranging 1–5 nmol; for high‑abundance sugars prepare 3–5 mixes ranging 20–100 nmol. Combine standards in the following groups: (1) xylose, fucose, mannose; (2) arabinose, galactose; (3) glucose, glucuronic acid; (4) rhamnose, galacturonic acid. Prepare each combination in triplicate. Dry the standard solutions under a stream of N₂ gas.

steps.title: Derivatize samples and standards
steps.instruction: For each dried sample or standard, add 15 µL O‑methylhydroxylamine hydrochloride (MOX) solution (30 mg mL⁻¹ in anhydrous pyridine). Incubate at room temperature overnight (use freshly prepared MOX, wear gloves, work in fume hood, use solvent‑resistant tips). After the overnight reaction, add 30 µL N‑methyl‑N‑trimethylsilyltrifluoroacetamide (MSTFA) and incubate at room temperature for at least 1 h but no more than 6 h before GC‑MS analysis.

steps.title: Perform GC‑MS analysis
steps.instruction: Inject 1 µL of each derivatised sample with a split ratio of 10. Use helium as carrier gas at 1 mL min⁻¹. Apply the following oven program: 150 °C hold 2 min; ramp to 250 °C at 5 K min⁻¹ (20 min); ramp to 320 °C at 15 K min⁻¹ (4.67 min); hold 320 °C for 3 min. Set inlet temperature to 250 °C, transfer line to 280 °C, ionisation energy to 70 eV, ion source temperature to 230 °C, and record mass spectra from m/z 40–500.

steps.title: Process GC‑MS data
steps.instruction: Define a compound list in the data‑analysis software (e.g., MSD ChemStation) containing all monosaccharides and the internal standard allo‑inositol. Use the standard runs to assign retention times and characteristic fragment ions (two peaks per monosaccharide may appear due to MOX stereoisomers). Select the appropriate peak (largest without interference) for quantification and define one target ion per compound (see Table 1 for examples). Integrate peaks automatically, then manually verify assignments and peak areas, correcting any errors. Re‑integrate if necessary and export the quantitative data (e.g., to Excel) for further analysis.
